page: Microsoft Azure DC64es_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the DCEV6 family, powered by an Intel processor with x86_64 architecture. This server features 64 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides dedicated CPU allocation to ensure consistent compute performance without resource contention from other tenants.

This server does not include local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via external block storage. It is Premium Storage capable, allowing users to attach high-performance remote SSDs to handle intensive disk operations. The instance does not feature any GPUs, making it unsuitable for hardware-accelerated graphics or deep learning workloads. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the DC64es_v6 offers a dense allocation of dedicated Intel compute cores and memory, making it a balanced option for enterprise workloads that require reliable CPU performance and a substantial memory footprint without the overhead of local NVMe drives.

The DC64es_v6 is designed for enterprise-grade workloads, including relational databases, memory-intensive applications, and large-scale web serving. Its dedicated 64 vCPUs and 256.0 GB of RAM make it well-suited for running application servers, enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, and containerized microservices that require stable, non-burstable compute resources.
